title: SeaSure
description: Boat owners describe a problem with text or photos, and SeaSure’s answer takes that boat’s equipment and service records into account. Repairs that need a professional go out as a service request.
detail: SeaSure organizes vessel knowledge around a boat’s systems, installed equipment, manuals, service history, and current issues. Its AI assistance connects that context to troubleshooting and maintenance workflows, helping owners understand a problem and carry useful diagnostic information into professional service.

caseStudy.roleContext: Lihon’s role on SeaSure was AI & Backend Engineer. The overview below describes the product as a whole.
caseStudy.challenge: Boat troubleshooting depends on the specific vessel, installed equipment, documentation, and service history. The product challenge is to keep that information connected as an owner describes an issue and seeks maintenance or professional help.
caseStudy.engineeringContext: The public product materials describe vessel-aware assistance, multiple input formats, persistent records, and service handoffs. The diagram maps how those parts relate.
caseStudy.evidenceSummary: The official website and app listing describe the features covered on this page.

architecture.alt: Conceptual SeaSure flow: vessel context and owner observations inform troubleshooting, with connections to maintenance records and professional service requests.
architecture.caption: Illustrative product flow based on public SeaSure materials. Component boundaries are conceptual, not evidence of deployed architecture.

technicalSections.title: Vessel-aware context and knowledge retrieval
body: A useful marine assistant needs the identity of the boat, its installed equipment, the relevant documentation, and its service history. SeaSure’s product presents these as connected context around the vessel, extending from a system to its manufacturer, model, component, and records.

This gives troubleshooting a specific information boundary: an engine question, an electrical issue, and a navigation problem can be interpreted against different equipment and documentation contexts.

technicalSections.title: Multimodal troubleshooting
body: The public product supports text, photos, documents, audio, video, and live video in its marine assistance experience. The app listing describes specialized AI guidance across engines, electrical systems, hull, navigation, plumbing, and safety.
Whatever the owner sends should stay tied to the same vessel and its documents until the problem is solved.

technicalSections.title: Maintenance records and professional handoff
body: The Captain’s Binder and service-record features organize manuals, registration, surveys, repairs, and maintenance events. When professional assistance is needed, SeaSure carries the boat and diagnostic context into a service request.
This connects conversational assistance to persistent operational records and a real service workflow, rather than leaving the result as an isolated answer.

technicalSections.title: From question to service request
body: The owner’s troubleshooting conversation and the boat’s records sit in the same product. A marine professional who takes the job gets that context with the request, so the owner should not need to explain the problem twice.

sources.title: SeaSure: official app listing and capabilities

title: Projuno
description: Commercial fit-out teams keep variations and invoices in Projuno, with a record of who changed each item and why. Juno AI answers questions about that project data.
detail: Projuno brings work orders, variations, invoices, project financials, and compliance information into a connected workspace for commercial fit-out teams. Juno AI supports project questions and workflow automation, while traceable records preserve the context behind changes, claims, and project activity.

caseStudy.roleContext: Lihon worked on Projuno as AI & Backend Engineer. This page covers the wider product.
caseStudy.challenge: Construction teams need to follow work, changes, invoices, and supporting evidence across a project. The product challenge is to connect those records so administrative assistance and commercial review use consistent project context.
caseStudy.engineeringContext: The public product describes connected project operations, Juno AI, financial views, and traceable changes. The diagram groups those capabilities.
caseStudy.evidenceSummary: The official product site and service terms describe the features covered here.

architecture.alt: Conceptual Projuno flow: work orders, variations, and invoices connect through project context to Juno AI assistance and commercial review.
architecture.caption: Illustrative product flow based on public Projuno materials. It shows relationships between capabilities, not a verified production architecture.

technicalSections.title: Connected construction operations
body: The platform connects project activity with financial and compliance data. Work orders, day dockets, variations, and invoices become part of a common operational view, helping commercial fit-out teams follow scope and revenue through the project lifecycle.

technicalSections.title: AI-assisted workflow orchestration
body: Juno AI answers questions about project information and supports customized administrative workflows. The official product also describes an AI caller for collecting updates from teams and suppliers.
Context should not get lost when information moves from a person into a project record or into an automated step.

technicalSections.title: Change traceability and evidence
body: Projuno emphasizes knowing who changed an item, why it changed, and what evidence supports a claim. Traceable records connect changes with project context and help teams keep supporting information available for commercial review.

technicalSections.title: Financial visibility and integration boundaries
body: Project financial views connect scope progress with variations, invoices, budgets, and margins. The public offering also lists Xero and MYOB integrations and multi-company management, extending the operational workflow beyond a single project workspace.
On the backend, that means every workflow reads the same version of a project’s scope and commercial records.

technicalSections.title: Less back-and-forth on changes
body: Projuno keeps variations, invoices and their supporting evidence in one place. The intent is fewer follow-up questions when someone asks what changed and what it cost.

title: Dr. Infinity
description: A documented clinical AI design combining medical evidence retrieval, source-linked responses, and local de-identification.
detail: Dr. Infinity approaches clinical AI through evidence retrieval, medical knowledge representation, and information governance. The supplied technical architecture separates local de-identification, hybrid retrieval, domain-adapted inference, and output verification to produce structured, source-linked clinical knowledge responses.
stack: Concurrent vector and medical knowledge-graph retrieval; MeSH and SNOMED CT relationships; domain-adapted LLM synthesis; local in-memory de-identification
visualAlt: Dr. Infinity medical knowledge graph and evidence retrieval concept illustration

caseStudy.roleContext: Lihon’s listed role is AI & Backend Engineer. The technical discussion follows a supplied project brief; individual deliverables and ownership boundaries are not documented here.
caseStudy.challenge: Clinical knowledge questions need relevant evidence, traceable citations, and careful handling of sensitive inputs. The documented design addresses how retrieval, synthesis, and verification can work together while limiting unnecessary exposure of patient information.
caseStudy.engineeringContext: The supplied brief separates local de-identification, concurrent vector and medical-graph retrieval, domain-adapted synthesis, and verification. The diagram summarizes that documented design. It does not establish clinical validation, measured latency, privacy compliance, or deployment behavior.
caseStudy.evidenceSummary: The architecture is described in the project technical brief supplied by Lihon in October 2026. The brief is listed below but is not published here. The project website is available separately; no benchmark report, clinical validation, or individual contribution record is included.

architecture.alt: Documented Dr. Infinity design: local de-identification precedes concurrent vector and medical knowledge-graph retrieval, followed by synthesis and verification of source-linked findings.
architecture.caption: Illustrative diagram of the supplied technical brief. This is documented design, not proof of production behavior or clinical validation.

technicalSections.title: Hybrid retrieval and medical knowledge graphs
body: The technical brief describes concurrent retrieval from a vector index and a structured medical knowledge graph. Semantic similarity retrieves relevant passages, while MeSH and SNOMED CT relationships connect clinical entities and support graph traversal across medical concepts.

Combining these retrieval paths allows evidence selection to consider both the language of a question and the relationships between concepts. Retrieved context can then be cross-referenced before it reaches the language-model synthesis stage.

technicalSections.title: Efficient retrieval-augmented generation
body: Retrieval and generation are decoupled in the documented architecture. Vector and graph lookups run concurrently, reducing the amount of retrieval work that must happen sequentially before evidence can be assembled for inference.

The documented retrieval design targets sub-50 ms index responses. Parallel retrieval, focused context selection, and a staged evidence-to-synthesis pipeline establish the latency budget and the boundaries between indexing, evidence assembly, and generation.

technicalSections.title: Domain-adapted synthesis and multi-agent reasoning
body: The project documentation describes domain-adapted language models working with medical literature and cross-referenced findings. PubMed, FDA labels, and peer-reviewed journals are identified as evidence sources, with medical fine-tuning and multi-agent reasoning included in the design.

The synthesis stage turns retrieved material into structured findings while preserving the relationship to supporting evidence. This treats retrieval quality, clinical vocabulary, and response structure as explicit system concerns.

technicalSections.title: Evidence grounding, provenance, and verification
body: Line-item citations, source provenance, automated source indexing, and audit metadata make generated statements traceable to retrieved literature. A verification layer is described as checking assertions against supporting material before the final response is assembled.

These mechanisms support inspectable clinical knowledge workflows: the response, its source context, and the evidence path can be reviewed together. Grounding and audit metadata make retrieval decisions visible throughout the synthesis pipeline.

technicalSections.title: Privacy-aware ingestion and deployment boundaries
body: The supplied design describes local, in-memory de-identification of the 18 HIPAA Safe Harbor identifier categories before outbound transmission. It also specifies AES-256-protected payloads, avoidance of raw EHR storage, and a zero-retention architecture.

Private-cloud and on-premise deployment options address institutional control over clinical information and EHR data sovereignty. These deployment boundaries complement local de-identification, encrypted payloads, and retention controls in the documented privacy architecture.

technicalSections.title: Expected practical benefit
body: Combining retrieved medical passages with knowledge-graph relationships is intended to make supporting evidence easier to inspect. Local de-identification is intended to limit unnecessary identifier exposure before outbound processing. These are design goals; clinical accuracy, privacy behavior, and performance have not been independently validated here.

sources.title: Dr. Infinity — Technical Highlights, pages 1–2
sources.note: Project technical brief supplied by Lihon Gebre, October 2026. Architecture descriptions are distinguished from performance targets and unverified reported figures.

title: WanduBot
description: WanduBot’s private search runs on SearXNG and lets users pick the upstream engines and privacy settings. A separate chat interface, WanduGPT, is part of the same product.
detail: WanduBot brings privacy-focused web search and a dedicated WanduGPT chat experience into one product ecosystem. Its SearXNG-backed metasearch interface makes retrieval configurable across general web results and specialist information sources, while exposing practical controls for search privacy, languages, and upstream engines.
stack: SearXNG-based metasearch; configurable upstream search engines; a dedicated WanduGPT conversational interface
visualAlt: WanduBot private search and conversational AI concept illustration

technicalSections.title: Privacy-first search architecture
body: WanduBot positions its public search service around untracked searching and states that it does not collect or store search data. The product emphasizes user control over search behavior rather than a persistent search-preference profile on the server.

Privacy is also visible in the interface: settings expose query submission, image proxying, tracker-parameter removal, and whether a search query appears in the page title. These are configurable protections, allowing users to choose how much query context is exposed through browser history, page metadata, and external resources.

technicalSections.title: Federated retrieval and search orchestration
body: The search interface identifies SearXNG as its underlying metasearch technology. A configurable set of upstream search engines gives users access to multiple information sources through a common query interface.

General web search sits alongside images, video, news, maps, music, IT, science, files, and social categories. Engine selection, displayed weights and time limits, and visible response and reliability information make source selection an explicit part of the retrieval experience.

technicalSections.title: Configurable query and result privacy
body: The preferences interface offers GET or POST query submission, an optional image proxy, and tracker URL cleanup. POST submission can keep the query out of the address bar; proxying image requests can reduce direct resource requests to image hosts; tracker cleanup removes configured tracking parameters from result links.

These controls serve different data-exposure boundaries and remain user-selectable. Browser-stored preference cookies preserve settings for convenience, according to the preferences page; that configuration storage is distinct from a behavioral tracking profile.

technicalSections.title: Language-aware retrieval and relevance controls
body: Language detection, multilingual search preferences, SafeSearch, autocomplete configuration, and category selection let users adapt retrieval to their research context. A technical question, a scientific reference search, and an image lookup can use different categories and source preferences.
Queries are handled the same way whichever engines a user picks, and each privacy option is easy to understand.

technicalSections.title: Conversational AI alongside search
body: WanduGPT supplies a separate public conversational AI interface alongside the search product. Together, the two surfaces cover source discovery and open-ended AI interaction.

Search configuration and conversational interaction form distinct product surfaces. The project brings source discovery, query controls, and open-ended AI interaction together around privacy-oriented information access.

technicalSections.title: Limits of the privacy settings
body: With these settings, users decide which upstream engines receive a search and how much of the query shows up in browser history and page titles. That gives control over some kinds of exposure, but it is not anonymity.

title: Legal RAG
description: Researchers ask a legal question in plain language and get an answer built from retrieved cases. Follow-up questions and case folders keep each line of research together.
detail: Legal RAG applies retrieval-augmented generation to legal research. The experience brings together natural-language questions, relevant-case exploration, recent research conversations, and case folders. Its engineering focus is connecting retrieved case context to useful answers while keeping follow-up questions and research material organized.
visualAlt: Legal research retrieval-augmented generation concept illustration

technicalSections.title: Questions to retrieved case context
body: The research workflow starts with a natural-language legal question and explores relevant cases. Retrieval-augmented generation connects the question with retrieved case context to support a grounded answer.

technicalSections.title: Conversational research and follow-ups
body: Conversational context supports follow-up questions within a research session. Recent conversations and search help researchers return to earlier lines of inquiry and continue exploring a topic.
As the conversation grows, a new question is read together with the earlier discussion and the cases already found.

technicalSections.title: Organizing cases and research conversations
body: Case folders and research conversations provide a way to organize related material around a line of inquiry. Relevant-case exploration and recent research activity remain connected within the research experience.

technicalSections.title: Reviewing a research thread
body: A saved thread can be reopened later with its retrieved cases still next to the answers. That makes it easier to check what an answer was based on.

title: Only Hers
description: Shoppers on the Only Hers storefront can ask an AI assistant about products. Its answers draw on catalog records that sync automatically from PostgreSQL into a vector database.
detail: Only Hers combines an e-commerce storefront with an AI shopping assistant. Product information from PostgreSQL is synchronized into a vector-based knowledge layer so conversational recommendations can stay connected to the catalog rather than relying only on static model knowledge.
stack: Django, PostgreSQL, vector databases, LangChain, React, Redis
visualAlt: Only Hers product-aware AI shopping concept illustration

technicalSections.title: Catalog-to-knowledge synchronization
body: Automated updates connect PostgreSQL product records to a vector database. This supports semantic retrieval over product information and helps the assistant respond using a catalog-aware context.

technicalSections.title: Conversational product discovery
body: The AI assistant supports product questions and personalized shopping recommendations. LangChain and a vector knowledge layer connect the conversation to product information, while the storefront and backend handle the broader shopping experience.

technicalSections.title: Answers about what the store sells
body: When a shopper asks about a product, the assistant answers from the store’s own catalog, so a newly added item can appear in recommendations once it syncs.

title: ALX Study with AI
description: A Next.js app that uses Llama 3.1 8B to turn study material into revision notes and flashcards, then quizzes the student with generated questions.
detail: ALX Study with AI uses a Next.js application and Llama 3.1 8B to help students work with learning material. The experience connects compact study notes, revision flashcards, and generated questions in one study workflow.
visualAlt: ALX Study with AI notes flashcards and practice concept illustration

technicalSections.title: Learning material to study artifacts
body: The application uses language-model generation to produce short notes and practice material. Separate study formats support reading, revision, and self-testing around the same learning topic.

technicalSections.title: Open-source web application
body: The Next.js interface brings the AI-assisted study workflow into a browser application. The public repository provides the project’s implementation context and source history.

technicalSections.title: From reading to self-testing
body: Every study format is generated from the same material, so a student can go from reading to self-testing without making revision cards by hand.

sources.title: ALX Study with AI: source repository

title: Academic Advisor AI
description: Students search for professors and get advice on choosing a major. Google Generative AI writes the replies from academic information retrieved through Pinecone.
detail: Academic Advisor AI brings professor search, major advice, and course planning into a Next.js application. Google Generative AI works with Pinecone retrieval to ground personalized recommendations in relevant academic information.
stack: Next.js, Google Generative AI, Pinecone, retrieval-augmented generation
visualAlt: Academic Advisor AI home page with cards for Find a Professor, Major Advisor and Course Planner

technicalSections.title: Retrieval-augmented academic guidance
body: Pinecone provides a vector retrieval layer for finding relevant academic context. Retrieved material supports generative responses for planning and professor discovery.

technicalSections.title: Multiple planning workflows
body: The interface separates professor search, major advice, and course planning so students can approach different academic decisions through a focused workflow.

technicalSections.title: Retrieval at small scale
body: The Pinecone index behind professor search holds about 9 KB of professor records, a demo-sized dataset that shows the retrieval step.

title: Whisper
description: A MERN chat app where Socket.io delivers messages live and MongoDB keeps the history.
detail: Whisper is a full-stack chat application built with MongoDB, Express, React, and Node.js. Socket.io supports real-time message delivery, while JWT-based authentication and database-backed accounts organize access to the messaging experience.
stack: MongoDB, Express.js, React, Node.js, Socket.io, JWT
visualAlt: Whisper real-time messaging and conversation concept illustration

technicalSections.title: Real-time application communication
body: Socket.io provides the event-driven communication layer for live conversations. React handles the messaging interface while the Node.js and Express application serves backend workflows.

technicalSections.title: Authentication and persistence
body: JWT authentication supports account access, and MongoDB stores application information for persistent messaging workflows. Authenticated sessions and stored conversation data connect access control with the messaging lifecycle.

technicalSections.title: Picking up a conversation later
body: Because messages are both sent live and stored, a conversation can be picked up again in a later session.

title: Inventory Management
description: Items can be added to stock from a photo. Google Generative AI suggests the category, and Firebase stores the inventory.
detail: Inventory Management combines a Next.js and React interface with Firebase for stock organization and real-time application data. Google Generative AI supports photo-based item entry and automatic categorization to reduce repetitive cataloging work.
stack: Next.js, React, Material UI, Firebase, Google Generative AI
visualAlt: Inventory Tracker dashboard with a category sidebar and buttons to add an item or upload a photo

technicalSections.title: Photo-based inventory entry
body: Item photos support an AI-assisted entry workflow. Automatic categorization helps convert a visual input into organized inventory information.

technicalSections.title: Real-time stock interface
body: Firebase and the React application support responsive stock-management views. Material UI provides interface components for managing the inventory workflow.

technicalSections.title: Less typing at intake
body: Fewer fields are typed by hand when the category comes from the photo.

title: AI Customer Support
description: Customers type a question into a web chat and get a generated reply. The Next.js app saves each conversation in Firebase.
detail: AI Customer Support is a Next.js application combining generated responses with stored conversation records in a Firebase-backed web interface.
stack: Next.js, JavaScript, Tailwind CSS, Firebase, AI
visualAlt: AI Customer Support home page, titled AI Conversation Hub, with a chat list and a Start New Conversation button

technicalSections.title: Conversational support workflow
body: The assistant accepts customer questions and generates responses. Saved conversation records keep follow-up questions connected to earlier exchanges.

technicalSections.title: Web application integration
body: Next.js and JavaScript connect the support interface with the application’s AI interaction. Firebase supports the application data layer, with Tailwind CSS used for the interface.
